findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime keys, breaking the new audit-log pagination path
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), copying Paginator's numeric-key implementation. The only place it is wired up, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is 'datetime' and the attribute is a datetime.datetime; math.ceil(datetime_obj) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls get_item_key on results of every non-empty page, so every request with ?optimized_pagination=true from an eligible user (superuser or member with global access) returns a 500 as soon as the organization has any audit log rows. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting epoch-millis back to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so even if the first page worked, subsequent pages would compare a datetime column against an integer. The 'optimized' path is completely broken as shipped; it needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion (or should not be used on this endpoint). Note this endpoint/paginator change is also entirely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer eviction).

findings.title: organization_context.member.has_global_access crashes when member is None, on every GET
findings.body: Line 71 evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally for every request to the audit log endpoint. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None when the request is not tied to an organization member — for example API-key or org-token authentication, where request.user is anonymous and is_superuser is False, so the 'or' short-circuit does not help. Such credentials can pass OrganizationAuditPermission via org scopes, and they will now crash with AttributeError ('NoneType' has no attribute 'has_global_access'), i.e. a 500 on this endpoint even when the optimized_pagination parameter is not used. Guard the access (organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access) and/or compute it lazily only when use_optimized is true.

findings.title: 'Advanced' negative-offset pagination relies on Django negative slicing, which raises
findings.body: The new branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (and the comments at paginator.py:179-181, 874-879 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27) claims the Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' and that negative offsets are a safe, supported optimization. That is false: Django's QuerySet slicing raises ('Negative indexing is not supported') for queryset[start:stop] with start < 0. Cursor offsets are client-controlled — Cursor.from_string happily parses a cursor like '0:-50:0' — so with enable_advanced_features=True any client can supply a negative offset and get an unhandled 500, and the advertised bidirectional-pagination feature cannot work at all as written. The feature should be removed or implemented explicitly (e.g. computing absolute offsets), and the misleading comments in paginator.py and cursors.py corrected.

findings.title: SET→ZSET type change on existing span-buf:s:* keys will WRONGTYPE during rollout
findings.body: The PR changes the value type of the existing span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (SADD here, SUNIONSTORE/SCARD/SSCAN elsewhere) to a sorted set (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data) without renaming the keys. Any buffer key that still exists as a SET when the new code deploys — segments not yet flushed, or orphaned keys with TTL up to redis_ttl (1h) — will cause WRONGTYPE errors in the ZADD pipeline, in the Lua script, and in the flusher's ZSCAN, making the consumer and the flusher error repeatedly on those traces until the old keys expire. Use a new versioned key prefix or otherwise migrate/flush the old keys as part of the deploy.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, corrupting eviction scores for duplicated spans
findings.body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls omit an explicit AGGREGATE, so members present in both source sets get their scores SUMMED. With at-least-once Kafka delivery, a duplicate span payload can already be merged into set_key and later be re-buffered under a recreated child/parent key; the next merge then doubles its score (~3.4e9 instead of the ~1.7e9 end_timestamp_precise). Since the score is only used for eviction ordering, duplicated spans are subsequently treated as the newest spans and are evicted last by the 1000-span cap below, skewing eviction and, with repeated duplicates, crowding out legitimate spans. Add 'AGGREGATE MAX' (or MIN) to both ZUNIONSTORE calls so scores stay idempotent.

findings.title: Redirect-follow limit silently reduced 10000→1000 and its explanatory comment deleted
findings.body: The redirect-chasing loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment documenting the consequence ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was removed. Segment trees whose redirect chain exceeds 1000 will now silently stop resolving: the incoming span is written to its own buffer key and the trace is eventually flushed as multiple split segments with outcome 'different'. If the lower bound is an intentional tradeoff to bound Lua execution time, that decision and its correctness impact should stay documented in the script; otherwise restore the previous limit.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead configuration; Lua eviction hardcodes 1000
findings.body: The only enforcement of the max_segment_spans constructor parameter (default 1001) — the span-count overflow check in _load_segment_data — was removed, and its replacement, the eviction in add-buffer.lua, hardcodes the threshold ('if span_count > 1000'). The configurable parameter no longer has any effect and even disagrees with the hardcoded value (1000 vs 1001). Either pass the limit into the Lua script as an argument or delete the now-misleading parameter.

findings.title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction during insert
findings.body: The headline behavior of this PR — capping a segment's buffer at 1000 spans by ZPOPMIN-ing the lowest-scored (oldest) spans during insert — has no test coverage. The test changes only add the new required end_timestamp_precise field to Span constructors. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment (including the path where a child set is merged via ZUNIONSTORE) and asserts the buffer is capped at 1000 and that the evicted spans are the expected oldest ones.
